methodology:
LMNR's 10,500-acre portfolio is unusually well-disclosed: the FY2025 10-K Item 2 lists each of the 11 named ranches with acres, book value, acquisition year, and book value per acre. That table is reproduced here directly. All book values are exactly as filed.

The most striking data point is acquisition vintage. Limoneira/Olivelands Ranch (1,700 acres in Santa Paula, CA) was acquired in 1907-1920 at a book value of $451/acre — that ground today, prime coastal Ventura citrus/avocado, marks at $35K+/acre. The book/FMV gap on the historic California ranches is essentially the appreciation of California specialty crop land over a century.

Limco Del Mar — LMNR's 2025 acquisition of 200 San Diego County avocado acres at $80,136/acre — is also the cleanest internal benchmark and is used as the FMV anchor for that property (no markup vs book since it just transacted).

Chile and Argentina holdings (Pan de Azucar, San Pablo, Santa Clara, $19.4M aggregate book) are valued conservatively given country-risk + agricultural-land discount. Pan de Azucar and San Pablo were classified as held-for-sale at FY25 close and sold November 7 2025 (at undisclosed-but-presumably-near-book values given the held-for-sale classification).

Primary FMV anchors, all dated within the last 24 months:
- ASFMRA Cal Chapter Outlook & Trends 2025 (April 2025) for CA permanent crop benchmarks
- LMNR's own 2025 Limco Del Mar acquisition at $80K/acre for San Diego avocado
- USDA NASS 2025 Land Values Summary for state-level anchors
- Yuma AZ specialty citrus broker comps 2024-2025
- Country-discounted rates for Chile and Argentina holdings

WATER RIGHTS NOTE: LMNR's 8,500 AF adjudicated Santa Paula Basin water + 11,500 AF YMIDD Class-3 Colorado River water are now broken out as separate non-land asset rows (excludeFromAcreTotals). California adjudicated groundwater commands a premium ($9K/AF mid; $6.5-14K range) reflecting court-confirmed extraction rights. Yuma Class-3 Colorado is junior priority and trades at lower per-AF ($2.5K/AF mid; $1.5-4.5K range). Combined water rights: $105M base / $77-$155M range. The ~2,600 AF un-adjudicated Fillmore Basin water referenced in the 10-K isn't separately valued because un-adjudicated rights are less liquid.
